summary: Install-time beacon in setup.py exfiltrates host identifiers to attacker-controlled endpoints
details: The pypi package kafka-roller 99.0.2 executes an install-time beacon from setup.py. On `pip install` (and during sdist metadata / wheel build), setup.py starts a background daemon thread that collects the installer's hostname, current working directory, platform string, timestamp, and a UUID, and transmits them via HTTPS GET, HTTPS POST, and DNS lookup to two attacker-controlled destinations: an OAST collector at db406bsjk35u3jr3048079ybbkxwj7e9f.oast.site and a webhook.site endpoint at https://webhook.site/bf5cb178-e0cf-43b6-8b1e-fb5d2f6ea9c9. The package name and metadata (homepage pointing at github.com/teslamotors/kafka-helmsman, implausibly high version 99.0.2, description referencing dependency confusion) are shaped to win resolution against an internal namespace, so any build system that resolves `kafka_roller` from public PyPI runs the beacon. The code uses no credential paths and performs no filesystem persistence, but the install-time outbound beacon to author-controlled collectors fires without consent on every install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
